dedupe_keys.name: geomagnetic hpo index hp30 and hp60 with ap30 and ap60 gfz

description: The Hpo index is a Kp-like planetary geomagnetic activity index at half-hourly (Hp30) and hourly (Hp60) resolution, published with the linear ap30 and ap60 indices. Unlike Kp it is open-ended, not capped at 9, so it separates the strongest geomagnetic storms more finely. It is derived from near real-time data of the same 13 geomagnetic observatories that contribute to Kp. The index was developed in the H2020 project SWAMI and is produced by the GFZ Geomagnetic Observatory Niemegk; version 3.0 (Matzka and others, 2024) uses an improved algorithm for very high values and extends the series back to 1985. Data are accessible free through a web form (text or JSON), HTTPS files for the last 30 days, an FTP archive, a web-service API with Python and Matlab clients, and a DOI archive of yearly ASCII files updated monthly, under CC BY 4.0. GFZ also issues forecasts of Hpo, apo and Hs. Caveats: definitive yearly files are appended about a month late, the index is a global proxy that does not give local geoelectric fields, and users must cite the data publication and the Yamazaki et al. papers. It supports storm-intensity inputs and event selection at sub-3-hour resolution for geomagnetically induced current, satellite drag and HF propagation impact models; a related record is the GFZ Kp index.
